messages:
maya: Observed pattern: brand-new shards often win routing due to zero queue and then overload. Need a principled mitigation (not ad-hoc).
vik: Two principled approaches: 1) deterministic shrinkage penalty based on sample_count. 2) probabilistic selection that injects uncertainty into choice.
eli: Also consider admit_tokens: limit concurrent warmup requests to cold shards. Keeps them from blowing up once they start getting traffic.
maya: Proposal: runtime primitives: shrinkage(p95, n, prior), entropy_floor(min_score), admit_tokens(k). Keep policy DSL unchanged, primitives live in runtime.
vik: Example: scorer { base: p95; adj: shrinkage(base, n, prior); score: max(adj, entropy_floor(0.1)) + cost*0.7 } and routing_policy { admission: admit_tokens(3) if n<50 }
eli: Implementation notes: shrinkage and entropy_floor must be O(1); use precomputed priors per model/seq bucket. admit_tokens implemented with lightweight counters and fallback to other shards.
ops-bot: Telemetry request: emit sample_count, prior_bucket, entropy_score, admit_tokens_in_use per shard. Dashboard templating available.
maya: Rollout plan: 1) sim: compare current vs shrinkage vs shrinkage+admit_tokens (2w sims) 2) shadow scoring 1w 3) canary admit_tokens k=2 on 1% traffic.
vik: Tenant controls: coldstart_mode = {conservative, default, aggressive} to let tenants opt into cheaper tiers. SLA-bound tenants keep explicit affinity.
eli: Risks: raising entropy_floor biases towards costly shards. Mitigate with small default floors and tenant opt-ins; monitor cost-per-token.
maya: Action items: sam similar? (typo) eli to implement primitives, vik to run sims, maya to build dashboard queries. We'll sync next arch check-in.
ops-bot: Note: file GH tasks and include dashboard links once ready.
